definition: Circumvent means to get around an obstacle — to find a clever route past a rule, barrier, or safeguard instead of meeting it head-on.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circumvent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circumvent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: To circumvent the new tariff, the importer rerouted its cargo through a port two borders away, where the crates were relabeled and sailed on as domestic goods.
Sidestep is milder than circumvent: you sidestep an awkward question in the moment, while circumventing takes planning — a whole route engineered around the rule itself.
Flout goes further than circumvent: to circumvent is to slip around a rule while leaving it standing, but to flout is to break it in the open and dare anyone to object.

To bypass is simply to go around — the highway bypasses the town, and no one calls it clever. Circumvent adds intent and ingenuity: the obstacle is studied, then outmaneuvered, and it is usually an obstacle somebody put there on purpose.

To sidestep is to dodge in the moment — a quick step around an awkward question at a press conference. Circumvent is premeditated: a route planned in advance around a rule, a fee, or a safeguard — engineering, where sidestepping is reflex.

Circumvent means to get around an obstacle — to find a clever route past a rule, barrier, or safeguard instead of meeting it head-on.

The district's new firewall blocked the gaming sites by name, so within a week the students had circumvented it: someone discovered that the library's own translation tool would fetch any page whole and display it, 'translated' from English into English.
Notice that nobody broke through the firewall or switched it off.
Circumventing is the art of the route around — the barrier stays standing, untouched and technically obeyed, while the traffic it was built to stop flows past on a path its designers never imagined.
Circumvent is the planner's word — cool, procedural, at home in legal briefs and security bulletins.
It passes no verdict by itself: you can circumvent a censor or your own school's firewall, and only context decides which was admirable.
Note what it always implies: the rule or barrier is left standing.
Repealing a rule removes it; breaching one breaks it; circumventing walks around it and leaves it technically intact.
In this unit's company, guile is the trait and a ruse is the trick — circumvent is the route.

The new ordinance seemed airtight: no food truck could park on a public street downtown for more than thirty minutes.
The council expected the trucks to scatter.
Instead, within a month, they had found a way to circumvent the rule without breaking it once.

Truck owners signed cheap month-to-month leases on private driveways and parking pads — a dentist's lot here, a church's side yard there — spaces the ordinance, which governed only public streets, could not touch.
An alderman complained that the trucks were violating the spirit of the law.
Their lawyer agreed cheerfully, noting that the letter of it remained unbroken.
By summer there were more trucks downtown than before, each one parked, entirely legally, a few feet from the curb the law had cleared.
